incidents.vector: Intrusion method not disclosed; Equinor says the attack did not involve a computer virus.
incidents.impact: Internal IT systems, including corporate email, were disrupted; oil and gas production was not affected and no evidence of data theft has been found so far.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to two of Japan's national supercomputers, Fugaku and Rikyu, operated by research institute RIKEN.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included registered-user details, research data taken from home directories, and SSH keys used to connect the supercomputers to outside services.

incidents.victim: Unnamed Silicon Valley technology and defense company (and its employees)
incidents.vector: A Russian national recruited via Telegram entered the US illegally and conducted physical and electronic surveillance of employees — photographing laptop screens, positioning devices near the company's office for remote access attempts, and using fraudulent identification documents.
incidents.impact: Employees were surveilled and in one case followed for nearly 30 miles; detailed profiles were compiled on at least three employees of the company, which supplies weapons used against Russia in Ukraine. The defendant was indicted on espionage, stalking, and identity-fraud charges.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency holders, gaming-platform users, and VoIP software users (Europe)
incidents.vector: Trojanized installers and lure files, including a fake Viber app and VoIP-softphone decoys, deliver a Go-based RAT and a Python-based infostealer to targeted individuals.
incidents.impact: Deploys the "Overlord" remote access trojan, the "Good Game" infostealer, and a multi-cryptocurrency clipboard hijacker; the RAT uses Solana blockchain transaction memos to store resilient command-and-control addresses.

incidents.vector: Details of the intrusion method have not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Coles says no customer data has been confirmed stolen so far, though the company cautions this assessment could change as the investigation continues.

incidents.victim: Two US-based organizations (defense-adjacent technology and NGO sectors)
incidents.vector: Phishing and stolen Super Admin credentials combined with an MFA push-notification fatigue attack gave access to a cloud productivity environment; stolen data and impersonation of victim employees were then used to socially engineer a second organization via encrypted messaging.
incidents.impact: Full employee directories, email archives, and cloud-drive files were exfiltrated from both victims; the group registered rogue MFA devices and passkeys to maintain access for several months and deleted Alert Center logs to cover its tracks.

incidents.victim: US hospitals, schools, and healthcare providers (multiple states)
incidents.vector: The "8-Digits Team," affiliated with the INC and Lynx ransomware operations, gained network access, exfiltrated data, and deployed ransomware before demanding payment.
incidents.impact: The group claimed to hold more than 50 terabytes of data, including over 70 million confidential health records, and made more than $500 million in ransom demands; a Kazakh national has been extradited from Italy to face charges.

incidents.victim: Uber (approx. 150,000 individuals); also Cursor and Notion customers
incidents.vector: A financially motivated group breached AI infrastructure provider Fireworks using a leaked access key, then used stolen credentials to compromise downstream customers, including Cursor's VS Code extension marketplace and a cloud storage bucket used by a third-party service provider to Uber.
incidents.impact: Uber confirmed the names and driver's-license data of 149,346 people were accessed; Cursor said up to 5,000 users may have downloaded a trojanized Claude Code extension; Notion also disclosed exposure.

incidents.vector: Hackers placed malicious code on the site's ticketing checkout page to skim payment data.
incidents.impact: Payment card numbers, CVV codes, and expiration dates were stolen from customers; Fandango notified state regulators of the October breach.

incidents.victim: Indian defense contractors, military personnel, and potentially defense-sector workers globally
incidents.vector: Fake job-recruitment websites impersonating defense contractors (Airbus, BAE Systems, Lockheed Martin, and others) lure victims into downloading a trojanized mobile app that installs GravityRAT spyware.
incidents.impact: GravityRAT collects contact directories, call logs, texts, and WhatsApp messages from infected devices; the campaign has been active for roughly 12 months.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric-vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised master car accounts registered through Chinese eSIM services used by car importers, then locked owners out of their vehicles.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed owners had their cars hijacked and held for extortion; the true number of affected vehicles is believed to be higher.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations using Optimizely, including CNN, BBC, Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, Salesforce, and GitLab
incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's web-experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into the "Project JavaScript" field of customer accounts, which was then served from Optimizely's own legitimate CDN.
incidents.impact: The malware swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data from checkout forms, stole cookies and screenshots, and delivered the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits to visiting iPhones and iPads; researchers traced roughly $7,500 in stolen cryptocurrency.

incidents.victim: 700+ French retail stores, supermarkets, butchers, and a slaughterhouse
incidents.vector: French officials attributed the attack to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh Cyber-Electronic Command, which compromised commercial refrigeration controllers.
incidents.impact: Refrigeration systems failed at hundreds of stores, spoiling stock and causing tens of millions of euros in losses; France is pushing the EU to sanction Iran over the campaign.

incidents.victim: Government entities across Southeast Asia, South America, and Europe
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing and custom loaders deliver the PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT remote access trojans, which use HTTP/3 (QUIC) for covert command-and-control.
incidents.impact: The group has conducted stealthy, long-term data collection and exfiltration against government targets since at least 2023, using a built-in operational safety switch and synthetic traffic generation to evade detection.

incidents.vector: The group hacks telco infrastructure and plants backdoors that run malicious SS7 and Diameter signaling commands.
incidents.impact: Enables collection of device data, subscriber location tracking, and interception of calls and SMS traffic on selected targets; active since early 2025.

incidents.vector: An attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider — and forgot to revoke — to access its cloud environment, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access.
incidents.impact: The intruder had access to Barracuda's cloud environment for nearly two days before being detected and removed.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole tokens across 11 different cryptocurrencies from Binance, in activity blockchain-analysis firms and the FBI attributed to the North Korean group tracked as TraderTraitor.
incidents.impact: Approximately $6.3 billion was stolen, the largest cryptocurrency theft on record; Binance got about $2.8 billion of the stolen stablecoins frozen, leaving roughly $3.25 billion unrecoverable, mostly in Bitcoin and Ethereum.
